claim: Genetically barcoded Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B. theta) strains were used to quantify population bottlenecks experienced during colonization of the mouse gut.
source: In this study, we used genetically barcoded Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B. theta) strains to quantify population bottlenecks experienced by a B. theta population during colonization of the mouse gut.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the experimental approach and objective of the study.

claim: There is an inverse relationship between microbiota complexity and the probability that an individual wildtype B. theta clone will colonize the gut.
source: As expected, this reveals an inverse relationship between microbiota complexity and the probability that an individual wildtype B. theta clone will colonize the gut.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the barcoding experiments.

claim: The polysaccharide capsule of B. theta is important for resistance against attacks from other bacteria, phage, and the host immune system.
source: The polysaccharide capsule of B. theta is important for resistance against attacks from other bacteria, phage, and the host immune system
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Acapsular B. theta loses in competitive colonization against the wildtype strain.
source: correspondingly acapsular B. theta loses in competitive colonization against the wildtype strain.
evidence: The abstract states this as an expected finding based on the importance of the capsule.

claim: The acapsular strain did not show a colonization defect in mice with a low-complexity microbiota.
source: Surprisingly, the acapsular strain did not show a colonization defect in mice with a low-complexity microbiota
evidence: The abstract presents this as a surprising finding from the experiments.

claim: Acapsular strains have an indistinguishable colonization probability to the wildtype strain on single-strain colonization.
source: as we found that acapsular strains have an indistinguishable colonization probability to the wildtype strain on single-strain colonization.
evidence: The abstract states this as an experimental finding.

claim: Acapsular B. theta shows a longer lag phase in the gut lumen.
source: acapsular B.theta shows a longer lag phase in the gut lumen as well as a slightly slower net growth rate.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from tracking in vivo growth dynamics.

claim: Acapsular B. theta shows a slightly slower net growth rate.
source: acapsular B.theta shows a longer lag phase in the gut lumen as well as a slightly slower net growth rate.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from tracking in vivo growth dynamics.

claim: As long as there is no niche competitor for the acapsular strain, the longer lag phase and slower growth rate have only a small influence on colonization probability.
source: Therefore, as long as there is no niche competitor for the acapsular strain, this has only a small influence on colonization probability.
evidence: The abstract presents this as an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The presence of a strong niche competitor rapidly excludes the acapsular strain during competitive colonization.
source: However, the presence of a strong niche competitor (i.e., wildtype B. theta, SPF microbiota) rapidly excludes the acapsular strain during competitive colonization.
evidence: The abstract states this as an experimental finding.

claim: The acapsular strain shows a similarly low colonization probability in the context of co-colonization with the wildtype strain or a complete microbiota.
source: Correspondingly, the acapsular strain shows a similarly low colonization probability in the context of a co-colonization with the wildtype strain or a complete microbiota.
evidence: The abstract states this as an experimental finding.

claim: Neutral tagging and detailed analysis of bacterial growth kinetics can quantify the mechanisms of colonization resistance in differently-colonized animals.
source: In summary, neutral tagging and detailed analysis of bacterial growth kinetics can therefore quantify the mechanisms of colonization resistance in differently-colonized animals.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Encounters with environmental and food-borne microbes can be transient or lead to long-term colonization.
source: Whether such encounters are transient or will lead to long-term colonization is influenced by complex ecological interactions between the invading species and the existing consortium, as well as the host's dietary habits and the physiology of the intestine (David et al., 2014; Wotzka et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Understanding factors determining colonization efficiency is crucial for developing microbiota engineering strategies.
source: A better understanding of the factors determining colonization efficiency is crucial in the development of microbiota engineering strategies (Donia, 2015; Pham et al., 2017; Sheth et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated as motivation for the study with supporting citations.

claim: Genetic barcode tagging of isogenic microbes has been used to study population dynamics of pathogens within infected hosts.
source: This has previously been used to study population dynamics of pathogens such as Vibrio cholerae or Salmonella Typhimurium within the infected host (Abel et al., 2015; Vlazaki et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as background with supporting citations.

claim: Barcode recovery and mathematical modeling can infer parameters such as growth, clearance, and migration rates.
source: Based on barcode recovery and mathematical modeling, it has been possible to infer parameters such as growth, clearance, and migration rates (Dybowski et al., 2015; Grant et al., 2008; Kaiser et al., 2014; Kaiser et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated as background with supporting citations.

claim: Barcode tagging can estimate the size of population bottlenecks during colonization, antibiotic treatment, or immunity.
source: as well as the size of population bottlenecks imposed during colonization (Abel et al., 2015; Li et al., 2013), antibiotic treatment (Vlazaki et al., 2020), or immunity (Coward et al., 2014; Hausmann et al., 2020; Lim et al., 2014; Maier et al., 2014; Moor et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as background with supporting citations.

claim: B. theta is a common commensal member of the human intestinal microbiota.
source: B. theta is a common commensal member of the human intestinal microbiota
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: Precise tools for genetically engineering B. theta are available.
source: the availability of precise tools for genetically engineering it (Lim et al., 2017; Mimee et al., 2015; Whitaker et al., 2017)
evidence: This is stated as background with supporting citations.

claim: B. theta is a strong candidate for introducing novel functions into microbiomes.
source: makes it a strong candidate for introducing novel functions into microbiomes.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for choosing B. theta as the model organism.

claim: Bacteroides species can use phase variation to modulate the expression of 3–10 capsular polysaccharide (CPS) operons.
source: A common feature of Bacteroides species is the ability to use phase variation to modulate the expression of 3–10 capsular polysaccharide (CPS) operons, leading to the production of distinct capsule structures (Porter and Martens, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: B. theta strains lacking a capsule engraft poorly in an existing microbiota when competing with CPS-expressing strains.
source: B. theta strains lacking a capsule have been shown to engraft poorly in an existing microbiota when competing with CPS-expressing strains (Martens et al., 2009; Porter et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as background with supporting citations.

claim: Deletion of all capsule gene clusters is not expected to negatively influence the growth rate of B. theta per se.
source: However, the deletion of all capsule gene clusters is not expected to negatively influence the growth rate of B. theta per se (Rogers et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as background with a supporting citation.

claim: Capsule deletion can affect B. theta survival on exposure to bile acids, stomach acid, antimicrobial peptides, or phage.
source: Rather it can affect its survival on exposure to noxious stimuli, like bile acids, stomach acid, antimicrobial peptides, or phage (Porter et al., 2017; Porter et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as background with supporting citations.

claim: Genetically barcoded B. theta strains were generated that are able to produce capsular polysaccharides (wild type) or not (acapsular).
source: we generated genetically barcoded B. theta strains able to produce capsular polysaccharides (wild type [WT]) or not (acapsular, with deletion of all eight capsular polysaccharide synthesis loci; Porter et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the experimental strains generated for the study.

claim: The genetic barcodes were linked to an erythromycin resistance cassette to allow amplification by cultivation.
source: The genetic barcodes were linked to an erythromycin resistance cassette to allow amplification of our barcodes by cultivation.
evidence: This describes the technical design of the barcoded strains.

claim: Frequencies of barcoded strains can be determined by plating for CFU determination, recovering colonies, and quantifying relative barcode frequencies by qPCR.
source: Frequencies of barcoded strains in a sample can be easily determined by plating for CFU determination, recovering all colonies growing in the presence of the relevant antibiotic and quantifying relative barcode frequencies by quantitative PCR (qPCR).
evidence: This describes the methodology for quantifying barcoded strains.

claim: Combining CFU and qPCR values gives CFU of each barcoded strain.
source: Combining these values gives CFU of each barcoded strain (Grant et al., 2008; Lim et al., 2014)
evidence: This describes the methodology with supporting citations.

claim: Acapsular and WT B. theta show similar colonization success during colonization of mice carrying low-complexity microbiota (OligoMM12 and LCM microbiota).
source: This revealed similar colonization success (i.e., encounter of similar population bottlenecks) between acapsular and WT B. theta, during colonization of mice carrying low-complexity microbiota (OligoMM12 and LCM microbiota).
evidence: This is stated as a key finding from the experiments.

claim: The probability of colonization dropped approximately 10-fold for WT strains colonizing the gut of mice with a complex microbiota (SPF).
source: However, the probability of colonization dropped approximately 10-fold for WT strains and 100-fold for acapsular strains colonizing the gut of mice with a complex microbiota (specific pathogen free [SPF]).
evidence: This is stated as a key finding from the experiments.

claim: The probability of colonization dropped approximately 100-fold for acapsular strains colonizing the gut of mice with a complex microbiota (SPF).
source: However, the probability of colonization dropped approximately 10-fold for WT strains and 100-fold for acapsular strains colonizing the gut of mice with a complex microbiota (specific pathogen free [SPF]).
evidence: This is stated as a key finding from the experiments.

claim: The acapsular strain competed poorly against the WT strain in competitive co-colonization in low-complexity microbiota mice.
source: Despite similar fitness on single-colonization of low-complexity microbiota mice, the acapsular strain competed poorly against the WT strain in competitive co-colonization in the same setting.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding from the experiments.

claim: The discrepancy between colonization probability and competitive fitness could be explained by a longer lag phase and very slightly reduced net growth rate of the acapsular B. theta.
source: This apparent discrepancy between colonization probability and competitive fitness could be explained by a longer lag phase and very slightly reduced net growth rate of the acapsular B. theta.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The longer lag phase and reduced net growth rate give WT B. theta a head-start to occupy most of the available niche, excluding acapsular strains.
source: This gives WT B. theta a head-start to occupy most of the available niche, excluding acapsular strains.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The barcoding system can be used to quantify the bottlenecks experienced by a steady-state B. theta population in the gut subjected to an acute inflammatory reaction.
source: The same barcoding system can also be used to quantify the bottlenecks experienced by a steady-state B. theta population in the gut subjected to an acute inflammatory reaction.
evidence: This is stated as an additional application of the methodology.

claim: Six barcode sequences previously developed and validated for Salmonella were inserted adjacent to an erythromycin-resistance cassette and a GFP or mCherry fluorescent protein gene.
source: Six barcode sequences, previously developed and validated for Salmonella (wild-type isogenic tagged strains [WITS]; Grant et al., 2008; Maier et al., 2014) were inserted adjacent to an erythromycin-resistance cassette, ermG (Cheng et al., 2000), and a GFP or mCherry fluorescent protein gene under a strong constitutive promoter.
evidence: This describes the construction of the barcoded strains with supporting citations.

claim: Untagged strains were generated by inserting pNBU2 carrying the tetQb tetracycline resistance cassette and a GFP gene into the same integration site.
source: Untagged strains were generated by inserting pNBU2 carrying the tetQb tetracycline resistance cassette (Nikolich et al., 1992) and a GFP gene under the control of a strong constitutive promoter into the same integration site (Figure 1A, Key Resources Table).
evidence: This describes the construction of untagged control strains with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Fluorescent proteins were included to permit later visualization of clones.
source: Fluorescent proteins (GFP or mCherry), expressed from a phage promoter with an optimized ribosome binding site, were included to permit later visualization of clones (Wang et al., 2000; Whitaker et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the rationale for including fluorescent proteins with supporting citations.

claim: Samples were plated on BHIS agar with gentamycin to determine the total B. theta CFU and on BHIS agar containing erythromycin or tetracycline to determine the total barcoded B. theta CFU.
source: Samples were plated on BHIS agar with gentamycin to determine the total B. theta CFU and on BHIS agar containing the appropriate antibiotic (erythromycin or tetracycline) to determine the total barcoded B. theta CFU.
evidence: This describes the methodology for quantifying bacterial populations.

claim: The relative frequency of each barcode among the recovered colonies was obtained by qPCR using primer sets specific for each barcode.
source: The relative frequency of each barcode among the recovered colonies was obtained by qPCR using primer sets specific for each barcode.
evidence: This describes the methodology for quantifying barcode frequencies.

claim: Serial dilution and recovery of barcoded strains in in vitro systems shows excellent resolution over five orders of magnitude.
source: Serial dilution and recovery of barcoded strains in in vitro systems shows excellent resolution over five orders of magnitude (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a validation of the methodology with reference to a figure.

claim: Anaerobic growth in BHIS media was near-identical in all the barcoded B. theta strains with median doubling time ranging from 78 to 90 min.
source: Anaerobic growth in BHIS media was near-identical in all the barcoded B. theta strains (median doubling time ranged from 78 to 90 min) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The barcoded strains maintained their relative abundances when all barcode strains were mixed and grown overnight.
source: Correspondingly, the barcoded strains maintained their relative abundances, as evaluated by qPCR, when all barcode strains were mixed and grown overnight (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: Whole-genome sequencing of the barcoded strains revealed a few synonymous and non-synonymous mutations.
source: Whole-genome sequencing of the barcoded strains revealed a few synonymous and non-synonymous mutations, as would be expected for the construction process of individual strains (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with reference to supplementary data.

claim: None of the identified mutations is expected to have a major fitness effect.
source: However, none of the identified mutations is expected to have a major fitness effect, consistent with our observed data.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the sequencing results.

claim: Small, random deviations in barcode distribution were observed in colonization experiments, consistent with uniform fitness.
source: These experiments revealed small, random deviations in the distribution, consistent with uniform fitness (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with reference to Figure 1E.

claim: There was a minor competitive advantage of the tetracycline expressing strains over erythromycin only in the acapsular strain in culture.
source: In culture, we found a minor competitive advantage of the tetracycline expressing strains over erythromycin only in the acapsular strain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: There was no significant competitive advantage of any antibiotic cassette after 2 days of colonization in GF mice.
source: However, there was no significant competitive advantage of any antibiotic cassette after 2 days of colonization in GF mice (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: A simple model based on antibiotic fitness effect data suggests a maximum error of twofold.
source: a simple model based on this data suggests a maximum error due to the antibiotic fitness effect of twofold.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The error due to unintended fitness effects is small compared to the relative competitive fitness of the acapsular and wildtype B. theta strains.
source: This is small compared to the relative competitive fitness of the acapsular and wildtype B. theta strains.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: B. theta colonization was probed in mice carrying three different communities: LCM, OligoMM12, and SPF microbiota.
source: we probed B. theta colonization in mice carrying three different communities: low-complexity microbiota (LCM) Stecher et al., 2010; Oligo Mouse Microbiota (OligoMM12) (Brugiroux et al., 2016), and SPF microbiota.
evidence: This describes the experimental design with supporting citations.

claim: LCM contains 8 strains.
source: These include two low-complexity microbiota models with a reduced set of strains (LCM: 8 strains and OligoMM12: 12 strains)
evidence: This describes the composition of the LCM microbiota.

claim: OligoMM12 contains 12 strains.
source: These include two low-complexity microbiota models with a reduced set of strains (LCM: 8 strains and OligoMM12: 12 strains)
evidence: This describes the composition of the OligoMM12 microbiota.

claim: SPF microbiota includes 12 families that include several species.
source: and the closest model for complete microbiota in laboratory mice (SPF: 12 families that include several species) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the composition of the SPF microbiota with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: The distribution of barcoded B. theta cells in cecum content was evaluated at 48 hr after initial colonization.
source: We evaluate the distribution of barcoded B. theta cells in cecum content at 48 hr after initial colonization, a time point shortly after the B. theta population in the cecum reaches carrying capacity (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental design with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: A simple 'initial' model was formulated that allows inference of a per-cell colonization probability for B. theta.
source: we formulated a simple 'initial' model that allows us to infer a per-cell colonization probability for B. theta.
evidence: This describes the mathematical modeling approach.

claim: The model assumes that B. theta cells undergo random killing during their transition through the stomach and small intestine.
source: The model assumes that B. theta cells undergo random killing during their transition through the stomach and small intestine, that is, the population experiences an initial bottleneck event.
evidence: This describes an assumption of the mathematical model.

claim: Surviving cells arriving in the cecum start growing and the clonal progeny can be quantified at 48 hr post-colonization.
source: Surviving cells arriving in the cecum start growing and the clonal progeny of these cells can be quantified at 48 hr post-colonization via a combination of plating and qPCR (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the model assumptions and methodology with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The distribution of barcoded bacteria introduced into the stomach of each animal is better approximated by a Poisson distribution than by a uniform distribution.
source: The number of cells of an individual barcoded clone in the inoculum, n0, is low in our experiments. Correspondingly, the distribution of barcoded bacteria introduced into the stomach of each animal is better approximated by a Poisson distribution of mean n0 than by a uniform distribution.
evidence: This describes a statistical assumption of the model.

claim: The probability of losing a barcoded clone can be considered equivalent to the fraction of barcoded clones lost across all animals.
source: The probability of losing a barcoded clone can be considered equivalent to the fraction of barcoded clones lost across all animals.
evidence: This describes a statistical assumption of the model.

claim: Experiments where some, but not all, tags are lost from the final population yield maximum information.
source: Correspondingly, experiments where some, but not all, tags are lost from the final population yield maximum information.
evidence: This describes an optimization principle for the experimental design.

claim: An n0 of between 10 and 100 was optimal for both wild-type and acapsular B. theta in LCM and OligoMM12 mice.
source: In the case of LCM and OligoMM12 low-complexity microbiota mice, an n0 of between 10 and 100 was optimal for both wild-type and acapsular B. theta
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding.

claim: In SPF mice, an n0 of around 500 was informative for WT, but 5000 CFU were needed of each acapsular barcoded strain.
source: In the SPF mice, carrying a complex microbiota, an n0 of around 500 was informative for WT, but 5000 CFU were needed of each acapsular barcoded strain.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding.

claim: There was no consistent advantage of re-isolated strains over ancestral strains in colonizing the cecum at 48 hr post-colonization.
source: There was no consistent advantage of re-isolated strains over ancestral strains in colonizing the cecum at 48 hr post-colonization (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: The absence of strongly beneficial mutations in surviving clones is consistent with the experimental observations.
source: consistent with the absence of strongly beneficial mutations in surviving clones.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Excluding data from any one barcode has no statistically significant effect on the estimates of β.
source: Excluding data from any one barcode has no statistically significant effect on the estimates of β, as calculated using barcode loss (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B) or variance (Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: B. theta loads in the cecal content at 48 hr post-inoculation were similar in LCM and OligoMM12 mice, but significantly lower in SPF mice.
source: B. theta loads in the cecal content at 48 hr post-inoculation were similar in LCM and OligoMM12 mice, but significantly lower in SPF mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The colonization probability of barcoded B. theta WT strains was lower in SPF mice (Log10(β) = –2.35 ± 0.14) compared to LCM (–1.50 ± 0.10) and Oligo (–1.54 ± 0.13).
source: The colonization probability, β, of barcoded B. theta WT strains, calculated using loss or variance methods, was also lower in SPF mice (Log10(β, colonization probability) ± 2 standard deviations = –2.35 ± 0.14) compared to the two LCM (–1.50 ± 0.10; and Oligo, –1.54 ± 0.13) (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to figures.

claim: The relative size of the final B. theta population is 100-fold lower in SPF mice, while the relative colonization probability is only 10-fold lower than in animals with a low-complexity microbiota.
source: Of note, while the relative size of the final population is 100-fold lower in SPF mice, and the relative colonization probability is only 10-fold lower than in animals with a low-complexity microbiota.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The size of the open niche does not linearly translate into colonization probability.
source: This indicates that size of the open niche does not linearly translate into colonization probability
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: In LCM mice, the total population size of acapsular B. theta and the probability to colonize were not significantly different to the WT strain.
source: Surprisingly, in LCM mice, the total population size of acapsular B. theta (Figure 2E) and the probability to colonize (Log10β: LCM, –1.43 ± 0.13; and OligoMM12, –1.49 ± 0.14) were not significantly different to the WT strain (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 6B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to figures.

claim: There was no measurable fitness benefit of CPS in gut colonization up to 48 hr post-inoculation in LCM and OligoMM12 settings.
source: There was therefore no measurable fitness benefit of CPS in gut colonization up to 48 hr post-inoculation in these settings.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Both the total population size of acapsular B. theta and the colonization probability were tenfold lower compared to the WT strain in SPF mice.
source: Both the total population size of acapsular B. theta (Figure 2E) and the colonization probability (Log10β: SPF, –3.65 ± 0.13; Figure 2F) were tenfold lower compared to the WT strain
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to figures.

claim: There is a strong fitness benefit of CPS in the context of a more diverse microbiota.
source: indicating a strong fitness benefit of CPS in the context of a more diverse microbiota.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: SPF mice do not have measurable IgA titers specific for acapsular B. theta.
source: SPF mice do not have measurable IgA titers specific for acapsular B. theta (Figure 2—figure supplement 7A)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: No lytic spots produced by phage specific for acapsular B. theta were identified from the cecum content of SPF mice.
source: nor could we identify lytic spots produced by phage specific for acapsular B. theta from the cecum content of SPF mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Short-term recolonization resulted in a larger B. theta population in the cecum than long-term re-colonization with an SPF microbiota.
source: Although short-term recolonization resulted in a larger B. theta population in the cecum than long-term re-colonization with an SPF microbiota (Figure 2—figure supplement 8A)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: The colonization probability was near-identical between short-term and long-term SPF recolonization groups.
source: the colonization probability was near-identical between the two groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 8B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Mechanisms restricting colonization of acapsular B. theta in SPF mice are either direct microbial competition and/or very rapidly induced host mechanisms, or a combination of both.
source: Therefore, mechanisms restricting colonization of acapsular B. theta in SPF mice are either direct microbial competition (e.g., via type VI secretion) and/or are very rapidly induced host mechanisms, or a combination of both.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Competitive colonizations with B. theta WT and acapsular strains reveal a gradient of competition with the WT winning over the acapsular strain.
source: This reveals a gradient of competition with the WT winning over the acapsular strain, obtaining a competitive index (abundance of WT over acapsular B. theta at the end of the experiment) of approximately 20 in GF mice, 100 in LCM mice, and 104 in SPF mice (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The competitive fitness benefit of CPS increased in proportion to microbiota complexity.
source: Therefore, the competitive fitness benefit of CPS increased in proportion to microbiota complexity
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The colonization probability β was lower for the acapsular B. theta strain when co-colonizing with the WT strain than when colonizing alone.
source: Interestingly, the colonization probability β was lower for the acapsular B. theta strain when co-colonizing with the WT strain than when colonizing alone (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Competition with WT B. theta results in both a lower total population size and increased clonal extinction in the acapsular strains.
source: This indicates that the competition with WT B. theta results in both a lower total population size and increased clonal extinction in the acapsular strains.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The net growth rate of acapsular B. theta (0.40/hr) is lower than that of WT (0.50/hr) with p<0.01.
source: Tracking B. theta CFUg–1 in feces over 48 hr demonstrated that the net growth rate of acapsular B. theta is lower than that of WT (Figure 3C, WT: 0.50/hr and acapsular: 0.40/h, p<0.01).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Detectable exponential growth of acapsular strain starts around 4.5 hr later than for the WT (WT: 3.2 hr, acapsular: 7.7 hr, p=0.02).
source: Interestingly, detectable exponential growth of acapsular strain starts around 4.5 hr later that for the WT (Figure 3D, WT: 3.2 hr and acapsular: 7.7 hr, p=0.02).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: There was no evidence of differential retention of acapsular and WT B. theta in the small intestine.
source: There was no evidence of differential retention of acapsular and WT B. theta in the small intestine (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Early killing prior to reaching the cecum can be largely excluded as B. theta WT and acapsular clones have a very similar probability of colonization in single colonizations of OligoMM12 mice.
source: We can also largely exclude killing prior to reaching the cecum as B. theta WT and acapsular clones have a very similar probability of colonization in single colonizations of OligoMM12 mice (Figure 2 and figure supplements).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data with reference to figures.

claim: The delay in detectable growth of the acapsular strain is observed both in competitive and single colonization of OligoMM12 mice, consistent with a classical lag phase.
source: In contrast, the delay in detectable growth of the acapsular strain is observed both competitive and single colonization of OligoMM12 mice, consistent with a classical lag phase.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The magnitude of the delay to detection is similar on single and competitive colonization with WT B. theta.
source: The magnitude of the delay to detection is similar on single and competitive colonization with WT B. theta (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E and F)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: Acapsular B. theta exhibits a classical extended lag phase in vivo, likely due to a longer adaption period for growth in the gut environment.
source: We therefore propose that acapsular B. theta exhibits a classical extended lag phase in vivo, likely due to a longer adaption period for the acapsular B. theta to growth in the gut environment.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: A model combining differences in lag phase and net growth rates quite well recapitulates the expected competitive fitness and colonization probabilities.
source: Combining these additional variables generated a model that quite well recapitulates the expected competitive fitness (Figure 3F) and colonization probabilities (Figure 3G)
evidence: This is stated as a result of mathematical modeling with reference to figures.

claim: The competitive fitness defect of the acapsular B. theta strains can be explained by a slightly slowed in vivo net growth rate, with a small contribution from an extended in vivo lag phase.
source: Therefore, the competitive fitness defect of the acapsular B. theta strains can be explained by a slightly slowed in vivo net growth rate, with a small contribution from an extended in vivo lag phase.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the modeling results.

claim: GF mice were monocolonized with a mixture of untagged and barcoded B. theta WT strains such that all tags were present with a roughly uniform distribution prior to intervention.
source: we monocolonized GF mice with a mixture of untagged and barcoded B. theta WT strains such that all tags were present with a roughly uniform distribution prior to intervention, that is, minimum loss, in the gut lumen prior to challenge (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental design with reference to figures.

claim: After 3 days of infection with attenuated Stm, the total B. theta population was reduced approximately 100-fold in feces.
source: After 3 days of infection with attenuated Stm, the total B. theta population was reduced approximately 100-fold in feces (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: The probability of an established clone to survive the acute inflammation challenge was approximately 1 in 2000 in cecum.
source: In addition, the probability of an established clone to survive this acute inflammation challenge was approximately 1 in 2000 in cecum (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The initial estimated population of 1010 CFUg–1 B. theta in the cecum is reduced to an effective population of between 106–107 clones during Salmonella infection.
source: This means that the initial estimated population of 1010 CFUg–1B. theta in the cecum is reduced to an effective population of between 106–107 clones, while maintaining a total population size of between 109–1010 CFUg–1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Challenge with avirulent Stm has a limited effect on total population density of B. theta.
source: Challenge with avirulent Stm has a limited effect on total population density of B. theta (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Avirulent Stm still induces a bottleneck of approximately 1 in 250 in the cecum.
source: however, it still induces a bottleneck of approximately 1 in 250 in the cecum, potentially due to subclinical inflammation induced by colonization with a noninvasive Enterobacteriaceae (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: Around 90% of the B. theta clearance observed in virulent Salmonella infections can be attributed to the strong inflammatory response induced.
source: Rather around 90% of the B. theta clearance observed in virulent Salmonella infections can be attributed to the strong inflammatory response induced (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: HFD feeding did not significantly change the cecum population size of B. theta.
source: HFD feeding did not significantly change the cecum population size (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: HFD feeding did not increase the loss of barcoded B. theta.
source: nor did it increase the loss of barcoded B. theta (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: Detecting loss of one barcode in one of the tested mice would occur with a bottleneck population size of between 109 and 1010 clones.
source: To calculate our limit of sensitivity with this system, we estimated that detecting loss of one barcode in one of the tested mice would occur with a bottleneck population size of between 109 and 1010 clones
evidence: This is stated as a calculation of the detection limit.

claim: A population contraction of up to tenfold would be within the experimental noise of the measurements.
source: that is., a population contraction of up to tenfold would be within the experimental noise of our measurements.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the detection limit.

claim: The current neutral tagging system is not sufficiently precise to detect the magnitude of population dynamics changes induced by HFD consumption in GF mice.
source: The conclusion of the data is therefore rather than the current neutral tagging system is not sufficiently precise to detect the magnitude of population dynamics changes induced by HFD consumption in GF mice.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: The fitness-relevant effect of capsular polysaccharide expression on colonization success depends on the microbiota context, rather than on host effects.
source: When analyzing the effect of capsular polysaccharide expression on the process of colonizing mice with different resident microbiota, we found that the previously shown fitness disadvantage of acapsular strains (Coyne et al., 2008; Porter et al., 2017) depends on the microbiota context, rather than on host effects.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental data with supporting citations.

claim: In mice with more complex microbiota (SPF), B. theta can be outcompeted by the resident microbiota.
source: However, in mice with more complex microbiota (SPF), B. theta can be outcompeted by the resident microbiota (Lee et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated as an observation with a supporting citation.

claim: Expression of CPS is important for interaction with or protection against other microbes.
source: it is also probable that expression of CPS is important for interaction with or protection against other microbes.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the experimental data.

claim: Co-colonization experiments with mixed B. theta inoculums recapitulate similar colonization probabilities for the acapsular strain as that observed in a complete SPF microbiota.
source: Intriguingly, co-colonization experiments with mixed B. theta inoculums consisting of WT and acapsular strains recapitulate similar colonization probabilities for the acapsular strain as that observed in a complete SPF microbiota.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental finding.

claim: Direct toxicity between the acapsular and WT strains can be largely excluded.
source: As direct toxicity between the acapsular and WT strains can be largely excluded
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: A small difference in net growth rate, combined with an extended lag phase, is sufficient to numerically explain the competitive fitness loss observed in acapsular B. theta.
source: Based on the data for competitive colonization in LCM mice, as well as the outcomes of our mathematical models, we can conclude that a small difference in net growth rate, combined with an extended lag phase, is sufficient to numerically explain the competitive fitness loss observed in numbers and colonization probability of acapsular B. theta.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental data and modeling.

claim: Feeding mice that are stably monocolonized with B. theta a fiber-less HFD imposes a bottleneck that must represent less than a tenfold reduction in effective population size at 3 days post-treatment.
source: Feeding mice that are stably monocolonized with B. theta a fiber-less HFD imposes a bottleneck that must represent less than a tenfold reduction in effective population size of the B. theta at 3 days post-treatment
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: B. theta rapidly evolves to adapt to dietary challenges in the context of a resident microbiota.
source: It has been shown that B. theta rapidly evolves to adapt to dietary challenges in the context of a resident microbiota (Dapa et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The observed mild population bottleneck imposed by HFD feeding might only manifest if B. theta competes against other gut microbiota members that are more resistant to bile salts.
source: Therefore, the observed mild population bottleneck imposed by HFD feeding might only manifest if B. theta competes against other gut microbiota members, for example, that are more resistant to bile salts (e.g., Escherichia coli, see Wotzka et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation with a supporting citation.

claim: Inflammation causes a population bottleneck in the infecting Salmonella population, but this is less pronounced than the one observed for B. theta.
source: Interestingly, inflammation also causes a population bottleneck in the infecting Salmonella population (Maier et al., 2014), but this is less pronounced than the one we observe for B. theta
evidence: This is stated as an observation with a supporting citation.

claim: The rapid killing/clearance of gut luminal B. theta is representative of microbiota suppression that underlies the loss of colonization resistance in Salmonella-induced colitis.
source: Therefore, the rapid killing/clearance of gut luminal B. theta seems to be representative of microbiota suppression that underlies the loss of colonization resistance in Salmonella-induced colitis.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The mathematical models are based on assumptions that are useful to simplify calculations but always risk introducing bias.
source: Our mathematical models are based on certain assumptions that are useful to simplify calculations but always risk introducing bias.
evidence: This is stated as an acknowledgment of the limitations of the modeling approach.

claim: Estimates of colonization probability, growth, and clearance rates give a good overview of the harsh processes with strong effects on the total intestinal B. theta population.
source: Nevertheless, recognizing these limitations, our estimates of colonization probability, growth, and clearance rates still give a good overview of the harsh processes with strong effects on the total intestinal B. theta population.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the utility of the modeling approach.

claim: Peak-to-trough replication rate analysis reveals the growth rate at the time of measurement, whereas neutral tagging reveals population dynamics parameters averaged over much larger time spans.
source: It should be noted that these techniques give different information: peak-to-trough replication rate analysis reveals the growth rate at the time of measurement, whereas neutral tagging typically reveals population dynamics parameters averaged over much larger time spans.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of different methodological approaches.

claim: Sequencing requires that the strain of interest is >0.1% of the total microbiota to generate sufficient confidence in the reads with reasonable sequencing runs.
source: While sequencing requires that the strain of interest is >0.1% of the total microbiota in order to generate sufficient confidence in the reads with reasonable sequencing runs, neutral tags can be used to examine very small populations.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of the limitations of different methodological approaches.

claim: Neutral tags can be used to examine very small populations.
source: While sequencing requires that the strain of interest is >0.1% of the total microbiota in order to generate sufficient confidence in the reads with reasonable sequencing runs, neutral tags can be used to examine very small populations.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the neutral tagging approach.

claim: Far more factors influence the interpretation of neutral tagging experiments than peak-to-trough ratios and therefore mathematical modeling is needed to understand the results.
source: However, far more factors influence the interpretation of neutral tagging experiments (bottlenecks, clearance rates, etc.) than peak-to-trough ratios and therefore mathematical modeling is needed to understand the results.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison of the complexity of different methodological approaches.

claim: Combining mathematical modeling with direct quantification of bacterial population dynamics can gain insight into the major phenomena influencing colonization efficiency.
source: By combining mathematical modeling with direct quantification of bacterial population dynamics, we can gain insight into the major phenomena influencing colonization efficiency.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the utility of the combined approach.

claim: The results help understand the different steps of B. theta colonization and serve as a proof of concept for studying other complex, multistep biological processes.
source: Not only do these results help us understand the different steps of B. theta colonization, but they also serve as a proof of concept for studying other complex, multistep biological processes using the set of experimental and data-analysis tools we are describing here.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the broader applicability of the approach.

claim: This raises the possibility to optimize colonization conditions to promote efficient engraftment of beneficial species into target microbiota.
source: This raises the possibility to optimize colonization conditions in order to promote the efficient engraftment of beneficial species into target microbiota
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the findings.

claim: This raises the possibility to better understand the processes of invasion of pathogens and the functional basis of colonization resistance.
source: or to better understand the processes of invasion of pathogens and the functional basis of colonization resistance.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the findings.
